label: late original-phase input of w (also t, m, 2, 0, z)
explanation: Fires almost only in the original (input) phase (99.9% of mass). It is never active at t<2, rarely at t=2-3, and its rate rises with position (orig_idx 8: 10.5x lift) and toward the end of the input (to_go 0 holds 44% of mass), so it is strongest in long sequences. It is strongly token-selective: w alone holds 48% of mass at 11.9x lift and makes up nearly all the top activations, often on runs like w w w right before <DEL>. Next come t (4.7x), m, 2, 0 and z; i and b are weak. The fire rate is higher on the first occurrence of a token. It does not fire on the delimiter or in the copy phase (22 activations in total). Predicate: one of {w,t,m,2,0,z} input at t>=4 in the original phase. It covers about 85% of activation mass but has only about 20% precision. Most of these token/position steps do not fire, and I found no clean history condition (prior digits, whether trigger tokens were seen earlier, previous tokens) that separates them. The unit looks like a graded function of input token identity plus accumulated position/state, not a crisp binary feature.
